en: The fastest wind speed ever recorded on Earth was 253 miles per hour during Cyclone Olivia in 1996.
A single handful of healthy soil contains more living microorganisms than the total number of people on Earth.
Pumice is a unique volcanic rock filled with air bubbles, making it the only rock that floats on water.
Because the water cycle constantly recycles moisture, the water you drink today is the exact same water dinosaurs drank.
Venus rotates so slowly on its axis that one single day on Venus is actually longer than its year.
Neutron stars are incredibly dense, meaning a single teaspoon of their material would weigh billions of tons.
The moon is slowly drifting away from Earth, moving about 1.5 inches farther away every single year.
In the deep ocean, a tsunami wave can travel underwater as fast as a commercial jet airplane.
A single strike of lightning is incredibly hot, reaching temperatures five times hotter than the surface of the sun.
Volcanic glass called obsidian can be fractured to an edge so sharp that surgeons sometimes use it for scalpels.
Saturn has such a low overall density that if you could find a bathtub big enough, the planet would float.
Our sun generates massive energy by converting four million tons of its own mass into light every single second.
